what_was_done: Closed the still-open hole in the allow-list's quoted-string rule. _QUOTED is now r"'[^'\x00-\x1f\x7f]*'" — the single quote is excluded from a quoted span, as the comment beside it and rewrite/spec/topics/caller-identity.md already said — so excluded characters can no longer ride between an outer pair of quotes with approval resting on the parser alone. The four recorded forms are refused by the regular expression by itself and are table cases now: 'vsdd survey 'a'b'' and 'vsdd survey 'a''b'' (adjacent-quote glue the old pattern read as one span), 'vsdd survey 'x'; id; 'y'' (the old pattern read 'x'; id; 'y' as one quoted argument, while sh, bash, dash and zsh run id after the semicolon) and 'vsdd survey ''$(id)''' (the old pattern read ''$(id)'' as one quoted argument, while the shells concatenate and run the substitution). Two new gates pin the layer separation the finding asked for: test_allow_list_regex_refuses_the_tables_on_its_own asserts caller._CALL_TEXT_RE.fullmatch(text) is None for every REFUSED_CALLS entry and every LEDGER_BYPASS_FORMS entry, so a hole in the regex can no longer hide behind the parsed shape the way it did when the tests only checked is_vsdd_call(parse(text)); and the property test gained a fourth position that drops junk drawn from the excluded characters plus the single quote between two quotes, opening with a quote so the span can never be one quoted argument. Proof by mutation: with the pre-fix caller.py restored byte-identically, three tests fail (test_allow_list_refuses_every_excluded_character, test_allow_list_regex_refuses_the_tables_on_its_own, test_property_junk_from_excluded_characters_never_approves); with the fix, all 24 tests in test_caller.py pass. Confirmation beyond the suite: a canary sweep ran 313 grammar-accepting texts (the allowed table plus 300 texts fuzzed from the grammar, quoted spans holding a semicolon, pipe, dollar, backtick, double quote, backslash, parenthesis, angle bracket and blanks) through /bin/sh, bash 5, dash and zsh with a logging vsdd in PATH and hid/id canaries beside it — each accepted text executed exactly the vsdd canary once, never a hidden command, under all four shells; the reverse probe shows the same harness logs the hidden run for the bypass text.

Left '=' out of the allow-list's program characters: the program alternative is now (?:vsdd|[A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]+/vsdd), so a first word shaped like an assignment can no longer match — 'FOO=/vsdd id' and 'a=b/vsdd survey', which a shell reads as an assignment followed by the command it runs ('id', 'survey'), are refused by the regular expression alone instead of only by the parser's leading-assignment check. The comment at the pattern and the comment beside _SAFE say why. The spec states the fact in the one place that owns it: rewrite/spec/topics/caller-identity.md's grammar bullet now reads 'a path of safe characters that ends in /vsdd and holds no =', with the reason in parentheses. Both forms joined the refused table and the runner test, so an agent's call in either form is shown to get no marker, no permissionDecision and no updatedInput; test_allow_list_regex_refuses_the_tables_on_its_own asserts caller._CALL_TEXT_RE.fullmatch refuses them without the parser. Proof by mutation: with the pre-fix caller.py restored, the table, regex-alone and runner tests fail on these forms; with the fix all pass. The four-shell canary sweep also covers assignment-shaped first words: no text the fixed grammar accepts runs anything but the vsdd canary under sh, bash, dash and zsh.
